standard.title: Perform music
standard.description: perform music using relevant vocal and/or instrumental techniques and performance skills
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can perform music in a range of forms they have learnt and/or composed in informal and/or formal settings (AC9AMU6P01). They have not yet focused on the full range of performance skills — posture, technical control, tonal balance, real-time problem-solving — or on planning and presenting performances that demonstrate stylistic understanding.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students perform music using relevant vocal and/or instrumental techniques and performance skills, demonstrating technical control and expressive understanding appropriate to the style and context.

nodes.label: Technique for solo and ensemble performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply relevant vocal/instrumental techniques in solo and ensemble performance contexts, maintaining posture and technical control throughout
nodes.minimum_width: Perform a piece with attention to at least two technical aspects (e.g. posture, tone production, intonation, rhythmic accuracy); identify what is working and what needs further development
nodes.typical_width: Maintain technical control across a performance, applying appropriate posture and technique for the instrument/voice and context (solo, ensemble, amplified); identify and address technical issues in rehearsal
wider: Analyse the performance practices of musicians identified as experts in specific styles — identify strategies for authentic stylistic interpretation and apply at least one strategy to their own rehearsal

Compare performance posture and technique requirements across different instruments or voice types used in the same ensemble — evaluate how technical choices in each part contribute to the ensemble's overall sound

response_modes.reason: Technical performance skills are built through deliberate, sustained practice — repetition with feedback is the learning mechanism. Students need repeated opportunities to practise technique with specific feedback rather than exposure to more performance contexts.

success_criteria: Demonstrates appropriate posture for the instrument/voice and context
Maintains technical control across at least part of a performance

nodes.label: Tonal balance and blend in ensemble
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can control tone and volume in ensemble performance to create a balanced sound, identifying and responding to imbalances in real time
nodes.minimum_width: In an ensemble performance, identify at least one instance where tonal balance or blend needed adjustment; describe what adjustment was or could be made
nodes.typical_width: Monitor and adjust tone and volume in ensemble performance to maintain balance; reflect on how balance affects the expressive quality of the ensemble sound
wider: Problem-solve a real-time tonal imbalance during rehearsal — diagnose the cause and apply a correction; evaluate whether the correction worked and why
Seek and use feedback from an audience or recording to evaluate ensemble balance — identify at least one aspect of balance that the feedback revealed that was not apparent during performance

response_modes.reason: Real-time ensemble listening and adjustment is a perceptual and motor skill requiring sustained practice. Students develop the ear-to-response feedback loop through repeated ensemble experience — breadth of ensemble contexts matters, but the mechanism is practice, not new information.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one instance of tonal imbalance in ensemble performance
Describes an adjustment that was or could be made to address it

nodes.label: Planning and rehearsing for performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a performance, identifying expressive skills and stylistic understanding to communicate, and rehearse with attention to those goals
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one expressive or stylistic goal for a performance before rehearsal; use that goal to focus at least one rehearsal session
nodes.typical_width: Plan a performance with multiple expressive and stylistic goals; rehearse with deliberate attention to those goals; adjust the plan based on rehearsal findings
wider: Plan and present an in-school performance — attend to how elements of music and vocal/instrumental techniques will convey stylistic understanding; evaluate the performance against the stated plan
Use rehearsal recordings to evaluate progress toward performance goals over time — identify turning points in the rehearsal process where goals were achieved or needed revision

response_modes.reason: Performance planning requires students to work backwards from an intended expressive outcome to specific rehearsal decisions. Scaffolding this reasoning (what do I want to communicate → what technical and expressive choices serve that → what do I need to practise) makes planning purposeful rather than procedural.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one expressive or stylistic goal before rehearsal
Demonstrates that rehearsal was shaped by that goal

nodes.label: Integrated performance with stylistic understanding
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can perform music that demonstrates technical control and expressive understanding appropriate to the style, in solo and/or ensemble contexts, for a range of audiences
nodes.minimum_width: Perform a piece for an audience in which at least two expressive or stylistic features are evident; reflect on what worked and what would change in a future performance
nodes.typical_width: Perform music in solo and/or ensemble contexts that demonstrates consistent technical control and stylistic understanding throughout; seek and use feedback to reflect on the performance
wider: Perform a range of music across different styles or forms, demonstrating that technique and expressive choices are adapted to each style rather than applied uniformly
Plan and present a performance that includes their own composed or arranged music alongside other repertoire — evaluate how performing their own work differs from performing existing repertoire

response_modes.reason: This is where technique, tonal balance, rehearsal planning and stylistic understanding come together in a single live performance for an audience. The coordination of these components under performance conditions — where real-time adjustment is required — is the learning that only performance itself can provide.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Performing across multiple styles and demonstrating style-specific adaptation is a genuinely rich extension — students who extend here develop range as performers and a deeper understanding of how stylistic intent shapes every technical choice.
success_criteria: Performs a piece in which at least two expressive or stylistic features are evident
Reflects on the performance with at least one specific observation about what worked and what would change
